messages:
Ant: Quick follow-up on the lease allocator RFC — hit a rollback race in staging where eviction overlapped a lease renew. Small-batch workload, non-deterministic but reproducible under load.
Sel: I saw a similar flake. Can you paste the minimal logs?
Ant: logs:
```
[evict] lease=4711 renew@1768888887 -> rollback
[kv] free-slot id=7 still referenced
[compact] removed slab slot=7
```
Jia: That suggests notify ordering: persist lease -> notify compactor. If notify is delayed, compactor reclaims based on stale free tokens.
Tom: Outline options: (1) make persist+notify sync (simple but adds latency), (2) monotonic lease-gen with CAS so evict verifies gen before reclaim (optimistic), (3) compactor consults authoritative lease table before reclaim (extra RPC per reclaim).
Ant: I prefer (2) as a middle ground. Renew increments gen and writes with CAS; evict reads lease.gen and only reclaims if it matches expected free generation.
Sel: Does our metadata KV offer compare-and-swap? Dedicated/private etcd do. Hosted global metadata may need a shim.
Jia: Tradeoffs: extra metadata ops and possible CAS retries vs correctness. We can accept spurious aborts with backoff. Need telemetry to measure abort and CAS fail rates.
Tom: I'll prototype the CAS path in allocator branch and add a microbench for renew+evict contention.
Ant: Telemetry counters: lease_reclaim_abort, lease_cas_fail, lease_double_ref_detect. ops-bot: feature-flag lease_metrics_v1 enabled in staging.
Sel: I'll add a unit test that injects a renew-delay to force the race and assert no double-free.
Jia: I'll audit hosted/dedicated metadata providers for CAS support and open an issue linking RFC #421 with perf targets: p99 latency impact <1ms, abort rate <0.1% under normal load.
Tom: Also consider tenant-level batching of gen increments to reduce QPS — but must preserve monotonic ordering across workers. I'll note it in the prototype.
Ant: Keep sync persist as fallback if CAS path is noisy. Action items: Tom -> prototype + bench; Sel -> telemetry + tests; Jia -> provider audit + issue; Ant -> update RFC with follow-up and metrics. Check-in Friday. :thumbsup:
